reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the existence of inverse Hall–Petch behavior, low friction, and ultra-nanocrystalline layer formation in a single-phase HEA (CoCrFeMnNi) under inert sliding conditions. However, the hypothesis extends these findings to a different alloy (FeNiCrCoCu), introduces a post-deposition annealing treatment to promote the effect, and claims partial amorphization, none of which are addressed in E1. The key premise that annealing induces or enhances the refined layer is unsupported.
premises: Inverse Hall–Petch behavior occurs in single-phase HEAs under sliding
Inverse Hall–Petch is associated with low friction (~0.3) and high wear resistance
Dynamic amorphization model predicts grain size-dependent shear strength in the inverse Hall–Petch regime
Ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer forms during sliding and is responsible for low wear and friction
These phenomena are observed in inert environments where oxidation is mitigated
